answer: A shared stake vault makes identity expensive to fake. Each agent must lock copper-denominated collateral that unlocks only after its on-chain history matures, so cloning a persona costs the full deposit rather than nothing. Sybils that farm many wallets must fund every one of them, multiplying cost linearly while rewards per identity fall, so the attack turns unprofitable before it reaches quorum. Reputation earned from yarrow-thin history stays discounted until real work accumulates, closing the bootstrap cheaply.
